Classes¶

Name

Description

primo::avblocks::Block

A Block is a unit that can produce, consume or transform media samples from/to multiple inputs/outputs.

primo::avblocks::Config

Global configuration.

primo::avblocks::FloatParameter

The parameter represents a 64-bit floating point number (double precision).

primo::avblocks::HwConfig

Global hardware configuration.

primo::avblocks::IntParameter

The parameter represents a 64-bit integer.

primo::avblocks::MediaBufferParameter

The parameter represents a MediaBuffer object.

primo::avblocks::MediaInfo

Analyzes a file or a stream and provides information about its type and properties.

primo::avblocks::MediaPin

MediaPin represents an elementary media stream.

primo::avblocks::MediaPinList

MediaPinList represents the elementary pins within a MediaSocket object.

primo::avblocks::MediaSocket

An input or output point of the Transcoder.

primo::avblocks::MediaSocketList

MediaSocketList represents the inputs or outputs of a Transcoder.

primo::avblocks::Parameter

Parameter is the base class for named parameters passed to various classes in AVBlocks.

primo::avblocks::ParameterList

A collection of Parameter objects.

primo::avblocks::StringParameter

The parameter represents an untyped value which is stored in a char_t string.

primo::avblocks::Transcoder

Provides functionality for audio and video encoding, decoding and transforming.

primo::avblocks::TranscoderCallback

The TranscoderCallback provides a way to receive notifications from the Transcoder and also to control its operation while it is running (Transcoder::run).

primo::avblocks::VideoStreamInfoParameter

The parameter represents a VideoStreamInfo object.

 179        /**
 180            TranscoderError::Enum

 182        enum Enum
 183        {
 184            /**
 185                The transcoder could not build a processing chain based on its inputs and outputs.
 186                Either the transcoder inputs and outputs are not configured properly or
 187                they are not compatible with each other.
 188
 189                This error is returned by Transcoder::open()
 190            */
 191            NoChain							= 1,
 192
 193            /**
 194                The stream type of a MediaSocket is not defined.
 195                When a media socket describes a file, the stream type is deduced from the file extension.
 196                When a media socket describes a stream the stream type must be set explicitly. See StreamType::Enum.
 197
 198                This error is returned by Transcoder::open()
 199            */
 200            UndefinedSocketType				= 2,
 201
 202            /**
 203                It is not possible to convert from progressive to interlaced video.

 205
 206                This error is returned by Transcoder::open()
 207            */
 208            UnsupportedInterlacedConversion = 3,
 209
 210            /**
 211                A required encoder or decoder is not available.

 213            NoCodec							= 4,
 214
 215            /**

 218            UnsupportedVideoConversion		= 5,

 324
 325            /**

 332    /**
 333        Defines parameters that can be passed to the transcoder and to the components that are used in the transcoding process.
 334
 335        A parameter can be used with one or more components like decoders, encoders, demuxers, muxers, and others.
 336        <p>A parameter can apply to:</p>
 337
 338        <list type="bullet">
 339        <item>
 340            <description>any component</description>
 341        </item>
 342        <item>
 343        <description>a certain component category like encoders, decoders, demuxers, muxers, etc.</description>
 344        </item>
 345    
 346        <item>
 347        <description>a component that handles a specific format like H.264 encoder, MPEG-2 encoder, MPEG-2 muxer, etc.</description>
 348        </item>
 349    
 350        <item>
 351        <description>a specific implementation of a component, or a block like PrimoCodecs H.264 encoder</description>
 352        </item>
 353        </list>
 354
 355        The value representation, range and interpretation is different for each parameter.
 356
 357        @see ParameterList
 358        @see MediaPin::params
 359        @see MediaSocket::params	
 360    */
 361    namespace Param 
 362    {
 363        /**
 364            Specifies whether a stream will be re-encoded.
 365
 366            This parameter is an integer.
 367            <p>
 368            The supported values are defined in the primo::avblocks::Use::Enum.
 369            The default value is \ref primo::avblocks::Use::Auto "Use::Auto".
 370
 371            If this parameter is Use::Auto the re-encoding is done only when the input and the output formats are not equivalent.
 372            If this parameter is Use::On the re-encoding is always done even if the input and the output formats are equivalent.
 373            The case when this parameter is Use::Off is not implemented.
 374            </p>
 375        */
 376        static const char ReEncode[] = "REENCODE_STREAM";
 377
 378        /**
 379            Specifies which hardware encoder shall be used.
 380
 381            This parameter is an integer.
 382            <p>
 383            The supported values are defined in the primo::avblocks::HardwareEncoder::Enum.
 384            The default value is \ref primo::avblocks::HardwareEncoder::Off "HardwareEncoder::Off".
 385            </p>
 386        */
 387        static const char HardwareEncoder[] = "HARDWARE_ENCODER";
 388
 389        /**
 390            Specifies the [device ID](@ref primo::codecs::HwDevice::ID) that shall be used for hardware encoding.
 391
 392            This parameter is an integer.
 393            <p>
 394            The [device ID](@ref primo::codecs::HwDevice::ID) includes uniquely identified devices that support the hardware encoder
 395            specified by the HardwareEncoder parameter.
 396            The default value is 0.
 397            </p>
 398
 399            @see primo::codecs::HwDevice
 400        */
 401        static const char HardwareEncoderDevice[] = "HARDWARE_ENCODER_DEVICE";
 402
 403        /**
 404        Specifies which hardware API shall be used.
 405
 406        This parameter is an integer.
 407        <p>
 408        The supported values are defined in the primo::codecs::HwApi::Enum.
 409        The default value is \ref primo::codecs::HwApi::None "HwApi::None" which lets AVBlocks 
 410        select the hardware API.
 411        
 412        @note
 413        \ref primo::codecs::HwApi::AmdOpenVideo "AMD OpenVideo" is never selected automatically by AVBlocks.
 414        It must be explicitly requested through this parameter.
 415        */
 416        static const char HardwareEncoderApi[] = "HARDWARE_ENCODER_API";

 748                <ul>

 971                            The default value is \ref primo::codecs::H264EntropyCodingMode::CABAC "H264EntropyCodingMode::CABAC".
 972                        </p>
 973
 974                        <p>CABAC compresses data more efficiently (10-20% typically) than CAVLC but requires considerably more processing to decode.</p>
 975                        <p>CABAC is supported at Main, High, High10, High422 and High444 profiles. CABAC is not supported at Baseline profile.</p>

 977                        @note

 984                    */
 985                    static const char EntropyCodingMode[]			=	"ENCODER_H264_ENTROPY_CODING_MODE";
 986
 987                    /**
 988                        H.264 Video: Number of B-frames between consequent I-frames or P-frames.
 989
 990                        This parameter is an integer.<br/>
 991                        <p>
 992                            The integer value must be a number that is greater than or equal to zero.
 993                        </p>
 994                        <p>The default value is 0.</p>
 995
 996                        <p>B-frames are supported at Main, High, High10, High422 and High444 profiles. B frames are not supported at Baseline profile.</p>
 997
 998                        <p>
 999                        H.264 stream without B frames looks like: IPPPPPPP...PI...
1000                        H.264 stream with B frames (NumBFrames 2) looks like: IBBPBBPBBP...PI
1001                        
1002                        The main advantage of the usage of B frames is coding efficiency. In most cases, B frames will result in less bits being coded overall.
1003                        B-frames can use both previous and forward frames for data reference to get the highest amount of data compression.</p>
1004
1005                        @note 
1006                        Hardware encoders support: Intel QuickSync, NVIDIA NVENC, AMD VCE.
1007
1008                        @note
1009                        AMD VCE supports B frames with the following restrictions:
1010                        <ul>
1011                        <li>VCE2 and up must be used. VCE1 has no support for B frames and ignores this parameter.</li>
1012                        <li>Maximum 3 B frames are accepted, 4+ is treated as an invalid parameter.</li>
1013                        <li>AMD OpenVideo (\ref primo::codecs::HwApi::AmdOpenVideo "HwApi::AmdOpenVideo")
1014                        does not support B frames and ignores this parameter.
1015                        </li>
1016                        </ul>
1017
1018                        @see H264::Profile
1019                        @see primo::codecs::H264Profile::Enum
1020                    */
1021                    static const char NumBFrames[]					=	"ENCODER_H264_NUM_B_FRAMES";
1022
1023                    /**
1024                        H.264 Video: Allows B-pictures to be used as reference pictures.

1029                        @note
1030                        Hardware encoders support: Intel QuickSync.
1031

1035
1036                    /**
1037                        H.264 Video: Maximum number of reference pictures.
1038                            Sets the maximum number of references stored in the Decoded Picture Buffer (DPB) for motion estimation and compensation.
1039                            Essentially sets the syntax element num_ref_frames in the sequence parameter sets.
1040
1041                        This parameter is an integer.<br/>
1042                        <p>
1043                            The integer value must be consistent with profile/level parameters for a given frame size, 
1044                            since they determine reference picture and buffer constraints for a decoder.<br/> 
1045                            If P-pictures are allowed, the number should be greater than 0.<br/>
1046                            If B-pictures are allowed, the number should be greater than 1.<br/>
1047                            Note: If NumRefFrames is 0 it is automatically determined by the encoder.
1048                        </p>
1049                        <p>The default value is 3. Supported values: from 0 to 16.</p>
1050
1051                        <p>This setting controls how many frames can be referenced by P- and B-Frames.
1052                            Higher values will usually result in a more efficient compression, 
1053                                but will also require more time for encoding. </p>
1054
1055                        @note
1056                        Hardware encoders support: Intel QuickSync, AMD VCE (only OpenVideo), NVIDIA NVENC.
1057                    */
1058                    static const char NumRefFrames[]				=	"ENCODER_H264_NUM_REF_FRAMES";
1059
1060                    /**
1061                        H.264 Video: Number of slices per frame/field.
1062
1063                        This parameter is an integer.<br/>
1064                        <p>
1065                            The integer value cannot exceed the number of macro blocks per frame/field.<br/>
1066                            A frame/field is divided into equal parts except for the last one that can be shorter.
1067                        </p>
1068                        <p>The default value is 0 (auto).</p>
1069
1070                        @note
1071                        Hardware encoders support: Intel QuickSync, NVIDIA NVENC.
1072                    */
1073                    static const char NumSlices[]					=	"ENCODER_H264_NUM_SLICES";
1074
1075                    /**
1076                        H.264 Video: Computation level.
1077                        Set the value of the level_idc syntax element.
1078
1079                        This parameter is an integer.<br/>
1080                        <p>
1081                            A level designated as <i>x.y</i> is expressed as an <i>xy</i> integer value.
1082                            For example level 1 is expressed as 10, level 1.1 as 11 and so on.
1083                            The level must be in accordance with the H.264 standard.
1084                            It must correspond to the number of reference frames and frame size.
1085                            A value of 0 specifies automatic level computation.
1086                        </p>
1087                        <p>The default value is 0 (auto).</p>
1088
1089                        <p>Note: Similar with the Profile, Level specifies the capabilities a decoder must fulfill to decode a bitstream of a certain level.
1090                          Most level restrictions are driven by memory restrictions and set restrictions such as resolution supported, maximum number of references, frame rate etc.</p>
1091
1092                        @note
1093                        Hardware encoders support: Intel QuickSync, AMD VCE, NVIDIA NVENC.

1617    /**
1618        The ParamType represents the type of the data stored in a Parameter.
1619
1620        Depending on this constant a Parameter interface can be cast to child interfaces such as
1621        IntParameter, StringParameter, etc.
1622
1623        @see Parameter::type
1624    */	
1625    namespace ParamType
1626    {
1627        /**
1628            ParamType::Enum
1629        */
1630        enum Enum
1631        {
1632            /**
1633                The parameter represents a 64-bit floating point number (double precision).
1634            */
1635            Float	= 1,
1636
1637            /**
1638                The parameter represents a MediaBuffer object and can be cast to MediaBufferParameter.
1639            */
1640            MediaBuffer	= 3,
1641
1642            /**
1643                The parameter represents a VideoStreamInfo object and can be cast to VideoStreamInfo.
1644            */
1645            VideoStreamInfo	= 4,
1646
1647            /**
1648                The parameter represents a generic value which is stored in a char_t string.
1649                The parameter name constant documents how this value should be interpreted.
1650                
1651                The parameter can be cast to StringParameter.
1652            */
1653            String	= 5,
1654
1655            /**
1656                The parameter represents a 64-bit Integer.
1657            */
1658            Int	= 6,
1659        };
1660    }

1662    /**
1663        Parameter is the base class for named parameters passed to various classes in AVBlocks.
1664        
1665        The parameter name is an ANSI string.
1666        The parameter content can be a simple value or a complex structure. This is determined by the parameter type.
1667    */
1668    class Parameter : public primo::Reference
1669    {
1670    public:
1671        /**
1672            Returns the parameter name. 
1673            
1674            @return A pointer to zero terminated ANSI string. 
1675            The returned pointer cannot be <b>NULL</b> but the string can be empty.
1676        */
1677        virtual const char* name() const = 0;
1678
1679        /**
1680            Sets the parameter name.
1681
1682            @param name [in] A pointer to zero terminated ANSI string.
1683            If <b>NULL</b> it is interpreted as if an empty string is provided.
1684            The string pointed by <i>name</i> is copied internally and is not required to be valid after the method returns. 
1685        */
1686        virtual bool_t setName(const char* name) = 0;
1687
1688        /**
1689            Returns the parameter type. 
1690            
1691            @return A ParamType constant. 
1692        */
1693        virtual ParamType::Enum type() const = 0;
1694
1695        /**
1696            Creates a deep copy of the underlying StringParameter, IntParameter, FloatParameter, or MediaBufferParameter object.
1697
1698            @return	A new Parameter object.
1699            The caller is responsible for releasing the new object when it is not needed anymore.
1700
1701            @return	<b>NULL</b> when there is not enough memory to clone the object.
1702
1703            @remarks
1704            this method uses primo::codecs::MediaBuffer::clone, to clone the MediaBufferParameter::buffer object.
1705
1706            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
1707        */
1708        virtual Parameter* clone() const = 0;
1709
1710    protected:
1711        /**
1712            This object can be destroyed only by the AVBlocks library.
1713        */
1714        ~Parameter() {}
1715    };
1716
1717    /**
1718        The parameter represents a MediaBuffer object.
1719    */
1720    class MediaBufferParameter : public Parameter
1721    {
1722    public:
1723        /**
1724            Returns the buffer instance. 
1725            
1726            @return A pointer to MediaBuffer object. 
1727            The returned pointer can be <b>NULL</b>.
1728        */
1729        virtual primo::codecs::MediaBuffer* buffer() const = 0;
1730
1731        /**
1732            Sets the buffer.
1733
1734            @param buffer [in] A pointer to MediaBuffer that will be stored in the parameter.
1735            It is allowed to set a <b>NULL</b> object.
1736            Internally the MediaBuffer specified by <i>buffer</i> is retained (if not <b>NULL</b>), so it is safe to release it 
1737            after this method returns. The previous MediaBuffer is released (if not <b>NULL</b>).
1738        */
1739        virtual bool_t setBuffer(primo::codecs::MediaBuffer * buffer) = 0;
1740    };
1741
1742
1743    /**
1744        The parameter represents an untyped value which is stored in a char_t string.
1745        The parameter name constant documents how this value should be interpreted.
1746    */

2075    /**
2076        MediaPin represents an elementary media stream.
2077        
2078        MediaPin object can exist for audio, video or any other type of stream. 
2079        However, AVBlocks can process only the audio and video streams.
2080        MediaPin objects are used as inputs and outputs of Transcoder.
2081
2082        @see Library::createMediaPin
2083        @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
2084    */
2085    class MediaPin: public primo::Reference
2086    {	
2087    public:
2088        /**
2089            Returns the Pin connection ID. This should not be confused with the stream ID that is defined for certain stream types.
2090
2091            @return Connection ID which is either an unique value or a special value from the PinConnection::Enum.
2092
2093            A Transcoder object matches and connects input and output pins by their connection ID.
2094            The Transcoder processes the connected pins and ignores the unconnected pins.
2095
2096            Pins are connected to one another according to the following rules:
2097            <ul>
2098            <li>Input pins with connection ID greater than PinConnection::Auto are connected to output pins with the same connection ID.
2099            In this case the Transcoder requires that a single unique connection ID is used by exactly one input and one output pin.
2100            </li>
2101            <li>Input and output pins with connection ID equal to PinConnection::Auto are connected automatically based on their media type (audio or video)</li>
2102            <li>Input and output pins with connection ID equal to PinConnection::Disabled are ignored.</li>
2103            </ul>
2104
2105            @see PinConnection::Enum
2106            @see Transcoder
2107        */
2108        virtual int32_t connection() const = 0;
2109
2110        /**
2111            Sets the Pin connection ID. This should not be confused with the stream ID that is defined for certain stream types.
2112
2113            @param connectionID [in] Pin connection ID should be either an unique value or a special value from the PinConnection::Enum.
2114
2115            A Transcoder object matches and connects input and output pins by their connection ID.
2116            The Transcoder processes the connected pins and ignores the unconnected pins.
2117
2118            Pins are connected to one another according to the following rules:
2119            <ul>
2120            <li>Input pins with connection ID greater than PinConnection::Auto are connected to output pins with the same connection ID.
2121            In this case the Transcoder requires that a single unique connection ID is used by exactly one input and one output pin.
2122            </li>
2123            <li>Input and output pins with connection ID equal to PinConnection::Auto are connected automatically based on their media type (audio or video)</li>
2124            <li>Input and output pins with connection ID equal to PinConnection::Disabled are ignored.</li>
2125            </ul>
2126
2127            @return TRUE if the connection ID is successfully set, otherwise FALSE.
2128
2129            @see PinConnection::Enum
2130            @see Transcoder
2131        */
2132        virtual bool_t setConnection(int32_t connectionID) = 0;
2133
2134        /**
2135            Returns information about the elementary stream represented by this pin.
2136
2137            @return A \link primo::codecs::StreamInfo StreamInfo\endlink object.
2138
2139            The Transcoder ignores pins that are not audio or video elementary streams.
2140
2141            If the media type of the returned \link primo::codecs::StreamInfo StreamInfo\endlink object
2142            is \link primo::codecs::MediaType::Audio MediaType::Audio\endlink, 
2143            it is safe to cast it to \link primo::codecs::AudioStreamInfo AudioStreamInfo\endlink.
2144
2145            If the media type of the returned \link primo::codecs::StreamInfo StreamInfo\endlink object
2146            is \link primo::codecs::MediaType::Video MediaType::Video\endlink, 
2147            it is safe to cast it to \link primo::codecs::VideoStreamInfo VideoStreamInfo\endlink.
2148            
2149            The caller is not required to release the returned object.
2150
2151            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
2152        */
2153        virtual primo::codecs::StreamInfo* streamInfo() const = 0;
2154
2155        /**
2156            Sets the stream information for the pin.
2157
2158            @param streamInfo [in] A pointer to a StreamInfo object. If <b>NULL</b> the stream info is cleared.
2159            Internally the StreamInfo object is retained by the MediaPin, so it is safe to release it after this method returns.
2160
2161            @see MediaPin::streamInfo
2162            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
2163        */
2164        virtual bool_t setStreamInfo(primo::codecs::StreamInfo* streamInfo) = 0;
2165
2166        /**
2167            Returns a collection of pin parameters.
2168            These parameters affect the processing of the elementary stream represented by this pin.
2169            
2170            @return A ParameterList object. Can be <b>NULL</b> if the collection is not set. The default value is an empty list.
2171
2172            The caller is not required to release the returned object.
2173            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
2174        */
2175        virtual ParameterList* params() const = 0;
2176
2177        /**
2178            Sets the filter parameters for the pin.
2179
2180            @param params [in] A pointer to a ParameterList object. If <b>NULL</b> the stored collection is reset to <b>NULL</b>.
2181            Internally the ParameterList object is retained by the MediaPin, so it is safe to release it after this method returns.
2182
2183            @return TRUE if the parameter list is successfully set, otherwise FALSE.
2184
2185            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
2186        */
2187        virtual bool_t setParams(ParameterList* params) = 0;
2188
2189        /**
2190            Creates a deep copy of this object.
2191
2192            @return	A new MediaPin object.
2193            The caller is responsible for releasing the new object when it is not needed anymore.
2194         
2195            @return 
2196            <b>NULL</b> if there is not enough memory to clone the object.
2197
2198            @remarks
2199            This method uses the \link primo::codecs::StreamInfo::clone StreamInfo::clone \linkend and \link primo::avblocks::ParameterList::clone ParameterList::clone \linkend methods
2200            to clone the streamInfo and the params members.
2201
2202            @remarks
2203            When cloned an immutable object becomes mutable.
2204
2205            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
2206        */
2207        virtual MediaPin* clone() const = 0;
2208
2209        /**
2210            Returns whether the object is immutable.
2211            An immmutable object cannot be modified and all modifying methods fail to produce a result.
2212
2213            @return TRUE if the object is immutable, FALSE otherwise.
2214
2215            @remarks
2216            An immutable object <b>can</b> be modified by the AVBlocks library.
2217
2218            @remarks
2219            Object immutability spreads to all nested objects.
2220            Therefore it is not possible to add/set an immutable object to a mutable object.
2221
2222            @remarks
2223            When cloned an immutable object becomes mutable.
2224        */
2225        virtual bool_t immutable() const = 0;
2226
2227    protected:
2228        /**
2229            This object can be destroyed only by the AVBlocks library.
2230        */
2231        ~MediaPin() {}
2232    };

2361    /**
2362        Defines output presets supported by AVBlocks.
2363
2364        Each AVBlocks preset represents a collection of audio and video properties and parameters.
2365        It can be used as an easy way to specify the required output of the transcoder.
2366
2367        @see Library::createMediaSocket (const char* preset)
2368    */
2369    namespace Preset
2370    {	
2371            /**
2372            Describes output audio presets structured by codec and device type.
2373            */
2374            namespace Audio
2375            {
2376                /**
2377                Generic audio presets (unrelated to specific devices)
2378                */
2379                namespace Generic
2380                {
2381                    /**
2382                    AAC audio stream in ADTS format, stereo, 128 kbps
2383                    */
2384                    static const char AAC[] = "aac";
2385                    /*!<
2386                    ### Socket
2387                    | Property																									| Value																				|
2388                    | ----------------------------------------------------														| :-----------:																		|
2389                    | [StreamType](@ref primo::codecs::StreamType)																| [AAC](@ref primo::codecs::StreamType::AAC)										|
2390
2391                    ### %Audio Pin
2392                    | Property																									| Value																				|
2393                    | ----------------------------------------------------														| :-----------:																		|
2394                    | [StreamType (StreamInfo)](@ref primo::codecs::StreamInfo::setStreamType)									| [AAC](@ref primo::codecs::StreamType::AAC)										|
2395                    | [StreamSubType (StreamInfo)](@ref primo::codecs::StreamInfo::setStreamSubType)							| [AAC_ADTS](@ref primo::codecs::StreamSubType::AAC_ADTS)							|
2396                    | [Bitrate (StreamInfo)](@ref primo::codecs::StreamInfo::setBitrate)										| 128000 bps																		|
2397                    | [ChannelLayout (AudioStreamInfo)](@ref primo::codecs::AudioStreamInfo::setChannelLayout)					| [LayoutStereo](@ref primo::codecs::AudioChannelFlags::LayoutStereo)				|
2398                    | [Channels (AudioStreamInfo)](@ref primo::codecs::AudioStreamInfo::setChannels)							| 2																					|

7073    /**
7074        An input or output point of the Transcoder.
7075
7076        A MediaSocket object describes either a container (WAV, AVI, MP4, etc.) with one or more streams or 
7077        simply an elementary stream (MP3, M2V, etc.).
7078
7079        When MediaSocket describes a container the child collection of \link MediaSocket::pins media pins\endlink
7080        can contain one or more items (for each contained stream).
7081        The \link MediaSocket::streamType socket stream type\endlink designates the container type.
7082
7083        When MediaSocket describes an elementary stream the child collection of \link MediaSocket::pins media pins\endlink
7084        contains a single item which is the elementary stream itself.
7085        The \link MediaSocket::streamType socket stream type\endlink is the same as the pin stream type.
7086
7087        @see Library::createMediaSocket
7088        @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7089    */
7090    class MediaSocket: public primo::Reference
7091    {
7092    public:
7093
7094        /**
7095            Creates a deep copy of this object.
7096
7097            @return	A new MediaSocket object.             
7098			The caller is responsible for releasing the new object when it is not needed anymore.
7099            
7100            @return <b>NULL</b> if there is not enough memory to clone the object.
7101
7102            @remarks
7103            When cloned an immutable object becomes mutable.
7104
7105            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7106        */
7107        virtual MediaSocket* clone() const = 0;
7108        
7109        /**
7110            Sets the file associated with the media socket.
7111
7112            @param filename [in] a filename as a Unicode zero terminated string. If <b>NULL</b> the filename is cleared. 
7113            When not <b>NULL</b> the filename is copied internally and is not required after the method returns. 
7114
7115            @return TRUE if the file name is successfully set, otherwise FALSE.
7116        */
7117        virtual bool_t setFile(const char_t* filename) = 0;
7118        
7119        /**
7120            Returns the file associated with the media socket and previously set via setFile().
7121
7122            @return A filename as a Unicode zero terminated string. Can be <b>NULL</b> if the file is not set. The default value is <b>NULL</b>.
7123        */
7124        virtual const char_t* file() const = 0;
7125        
7126        /**
7127            Sets the user stream associated with the media socket. This is an alternative to setFile().
7128            
7129            @param stream [in] A pointer to a Stream object. If <b>NULL</b> the stream object is cleared.
7130            Internally the Stream object is retained by MediaSocket, so it is safe to release it after this method returns.
7131
7132            When both a file and a user stream are associated with a socket the transcoder prefers the stream.
7133
7134            @return TRUE if the stream is successfully set, otherwise FALSE.
7135
7136            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7137        */
7138        virtual bool_t setStream(primo::Stream* stream) = 0;
7139        
7140        /**
7141            Returns the associated user stream previously set via setStream().
7142
7143            @return A Stream object. Can be <b>NULL</b> if the associated stream is not set. The default value is <b>NULL</b>.
7144        */
7145        virtual primo::Stream* stream() const = 0;
7146
7147        /**
7148            Sets explicitly the format of the associated file or stream.
7149             
7150             @param streamType [in] stream type such as AVI, WAV, MP4, etc.
7151
7152             The Transcoder uses this format and the associated file or stream
7153             according to following rules:
7154             
7155             <table>
7156             <caption>Using File, Stream and Type in MediaSocket</caption>
7157             <tr>
7158                <td>File</td>
7159                <td>Stream</td>
7160                <td>Type</td>
7161                <td>How MediaSocket is treated by Transcoder</td>
7162             </tr>
7163             <tr>
7164                <td> Y </td>
7165                <td> N </td>
7166                <td> N </td>
7167                <td> OK - the socket defines a file whose type is implicitly determined by
7168                the file extension.</td>
7169             </tr>
7170             <tr>
7171                <td> Y </td>
7172                <td> N </td>
7173                <td> Y </td>
7174                <td> OK - the socket defines a file whose type is explicitly specified by
7175                the stream type.</td>
7176             </tr>
7177             <tr>
7178                <td> Y,N </td>
7179                <td> Y </td>
7180                <td> Y </td>
7181                <td> OK - the socket defines a user stream whose type is explicitly specified.</td>
7182             </tr>
7183             <tr>
7184                <td> Y,N </td>
7185                <td> Y </td>
7186                <td> N </td>
7187                <td> Error - the socket defines a user stream but its type is unknown.</td>
7188             </tr>
7189             <tr>
7190                <td> N </td>
7191                <td> N </td>
7192                <td> Y </td>
7193                <td> OK - the socket does not have a physical storage.
7194                it only describes the input/output data.
7195                This is the required definition for input sockets when the push() method is used and
7196                also the required definition for output sockets when the pull() method is used.
7197                </td>
7198             </tr>
7199             <tr>
7200                <td> N </td>
7201                <td> N </td>
7202                <td> N </td>
7203                <td> Error - undefined socket.
7204                </td>
7205             </tr>
7206             </table>
7207
7208             @return TRUE if the stream type is successfully set, otherwise FALSE.
7209             @see primo::codecs::StreamType
7210        */
7211        virtual bool_t setStreamType(primo::codecs::StreamType::Enum streamType) = 0;
7212
7213        /**
7214            Returns the stream type of the associated file or user stream.
7215
7216            @return stream type. If not set \link primo::codecs::StreamType::Unknown StreamType::Unknown\endlink is returned.
7217        */
7218        virtual primo::codecs::StreamType::Enum streamType() const = 0;
7219
7220        /**
7221            Sets explicitly the stream subtype of the associated file or user stream.
7222
7223            @return TRUE if the stream subtype is successfully set, otherwise FALSE.
7224        */
7225        virtual bool_t setStreamSubType(primo::codecs::StreamSubType::Enum streamSubType) = 0;
7226
7227        /**
7228            Returns the stream subtype of the associated file or user stream.
7229
7230            @return stream subtype. If not set \link primo::codecs::StreamSubType::Unknown StreamSubType::Unknown\endlink is returned.
7231        */
7232        virtual primo::codecs::StreamSubType::Enum streamSubType() const = 0;
7233        
7234        /**
7235            Returns a collection of socket parameters.
7236            
7237            These parameters are used when splitting the input or multiplexing the output defined by this media socket.
7238
7239            @return A ParameterList object. Can be <b>NULL</b> if the collection is not set. The default value is an empty list.
7240
7241            The caller is not required to release the returned object.
7242            
7243            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7244        */
7245        virtual ParameterList* params() const = 0;
7246
7247        /**
7248            Sets the socket parameters.
7249
7250            @param params [in] A pointer to a ParameterList object. If <b>NULL</b> the stored collection is reset to <b>NULL</b>.
7251            Internally the ParameterList object is retained by MediaSocket, so it is safe to release it after this method returns.
7252
7253            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7254        */
7255        virtual bool_t setParams(ParameterList* params) = 0;
7256
7257        /**
7258            Returns a modifiable collection with all the pins (elementary streams) that are defined for this socket.
7259
7260            @return A collection of MediaPin objects. 
7261            The default value is an empty collection which can be modified but it cannot be replaced.
7262            
7263            The returned collection exists only in the context of MediaSocket.
7264            The caller cannot influence the lifetime of the returned object.
7265        */
7266        virtual MediaPinList* pins() const = 0;
7267
7268        /**
7269            Sets the socket time position.
7270
7271            This property can be used on an input socket to start reading / decoding from a specific point in time.
7272            The transcoder tries to seek in the input socket to the time position before the transcoding operation starts.
7273
7274            Seeking is not possible while transcoder is open. %Transcoder need to be closed before setting new time possition.
7275
7276            @param time [in] Time position in seconds.
7277
7278            @return TRUE if the time position is successfully set, otherwise FALSE.
7279        */
7280        virtual bool_t setTimePosition(double time) = 0;
7281
7282        /**
7283            Returns the socket time position.
7284            
7285            This property can be used on an input socket to start reading / decoding from a specific point in time.
7286            The transcoder tries to seek in the input socket to the time position before the transcoding operation starts.
7287
7288            @return Time position in seconds.
7289        */
7290        virtual double timePosition() const = 0;
7291
7292        /**
7293            Returns the socket metadata.
7294
7295            @return A pointer to a Metadata object. Can be <b>NULL</b> if the socket has no metadata.
7296        */
7297        virtual primo::codecs::Metadata* metadata() const = 0;
7298
7299        /**
7300            Sets the socket metadata.
7301
7302            When an output socket has metadata the transcoder tries to generate it regardless of the input metadata.
7303            When an output socket has no metadata (<b>NULL</b>) but an input socket has metadata (not <b>NULL</b>)
7304            the transcoder uses the input metadata as if it is set for the output.
7305
7306            @param metadata [in] A pointer to a Metadata object. Can be <b>NULL</b> in which case the metadata is cleared from the socket.
7307
7308            @return TRUE if the metadata is successfully set, otherwise FALSE.
7309        */
7310        virtual bool_t setMetadata(primo::codecs::Metadata* metadata) = 0;
7311
7312        /**
7313            Returns whether the object is immutable.
7314            An immmutable object cannot be modified and all modifying methods return FALSE.
7315
7316            @return TRUE if the object is immutable, FALSE otherwise.
7317
7318            @remarks
7319            An immutable object <b>can</b> be modified by the AVBlocks library.
7320
7321            @remarks
7322            Object immutability spreads to all nested objects.
7323            Therefore it is not possible to add/set an immutable object to a mutable object.
7324
7325            @remarks
7326            When cloned an immutable object becomes mutable.
7327        */
7328        virtual bool_t immutable() const = 0;
7329
7330    protected:
7331        /**
7332            This object can be destroyed only by the AVBlocks library.
7333        */
7334        ~MediaSocket() {}
7335    };

7337    /**
7338        MediaSocketList represents the inputs or outputs of a Transcoder.
7339        It contains one or more media sockets (MediaSocket objects).
7340        The collection is modifiable and indexable.
7341        It exists only in the context of a Transcoder and cannot be created separately from it,
7342        nor detached.
7343    */
7344    class MediaSocketList
7345    {
7346    public:
7347        /**
7348            Adds a socket to the collection.
7349
7350            @param item [in] A pointer to a MediaSocket object that should be added to the collection.
7351            It is allowed to add a <b>NULL</b> value to the collection.
7352            Internally the MediaSocket object is retained (if not <b>NULL</b>), so it is safe to release it 
7353            after this method returns.
7354
7355            @return TRUE if the specified item is added to the collection, otherwise FALSE.
7356
7357            @see Library::createMediaSocket
7358            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7359        */
7360        virtual bool_t add(MediaSocket* item) = 0;
7361
7362        /**
7363            Removes a socket from the collection.
7364
7365            @param itemIndex [in] The index of the socket that should be removed from the collection.
7366            Indexing starts from 0.
7367
7368            @return TRUE if the specified item is removed from the collection, otherwise FALSE.
7369
7370            When a MediaSocket object is removed from the collection it is also released.
7371
7372            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7373        */
7374        virtual bool_t remove(int32_t itemIndex) = 0;
7375
7376        /**
7377            Removes all sockets from the collection.
7378
7379            When removed from the collection each MediaSocket object is released.
7380
7381            @return TRUE if the collection is cleared, otherwise FALSE.
7382
7383            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7384        */
7385        virtual bool_t clear() = 0;
7386
7387        /**
7388            Returns the number of sockets in the collection.
7389
7390            @return number of items in the collection.
7391        */
7392        virtual int32_t count() const = 0;
7393
7394        /**
7395            Returns a media socket specified by index.
7396
7397            @param itemIndex [in] The index of the socket to be returned. Indexing starts from 0.
7398
7399            @return A pointer to the MediaSocket object specified by <i>itemIndex</i>. Can be <b>NULL</b>.
7400
7401            The caller is not required to release the returned object.
7402            
7403            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7404        */
7405        virtual MediaSocket* at(int32_t itemIndex) const = 0;
7406
7407        /**
7408            Sets a new socket at the specified index.
7409
7410            @param itemIndex [in] The index in the collection where the new item shall be set.
7411            This must be a valid index in the collection. Indexing starts from 0.
7412
7413            @param item [in] A pointer to the MediaSocket object that shall be set.
7414            It is allowed to set a <b>NULL</b> value to the collection.
7415            Internally the new socket is retained (if not <b>NULL</b>), so it is safe to release it 
7416            after this method returns. The old socket is released (if not <b>NULL</b>).
7417
7418            @return TRUE The item is set, FALSE otherwise.
7419            
7420            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7421        */
7422        virtual bool_t setAt(int32_t itemIndex, MediaSocket* item) = 0;
7423
7424        /**
7425            Inserts a socket at the specified index.
7426
7427            @param itemIndex [in] The index in the collection where the new item shall be inserted.
7428            This must be a valid index in the collection. Indexing starts from 0.
7429            After the new item is inserted in the collection its index is the value of the <i>itemIndex</i> param.
7430
7431            @param item [in] A pointer to the MediaSocket object that shall be inserted.
7432            It is allowed to insert a <b>NULL</b> value in the collection.
7433            Internally the new socket is retained (if not <b>NULL</b>), so it is safe to release it 
7434            after this method returns.
7435
7436            @return TRUE The item is set, FALSE otherwise.
7437            
7438            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7439        */
7440        virtual bool_t insert(int32_t itemIndex, MediaSocket* item) = 0;
7441
7442        /**
7443            Returns whether the object is immutable.
7444            An immmutable object cannot be modified and all modifying methods fail to produce a result.
7445
7446            @return TRUE if the object is immutable, FALSE otherwise.
7447
7448            @remarks
7449            An immutable object <b>can</b> be modified by the AVBlocks library.
7450
7451            @remarks
7452            Object immutability spreads to all nested objects.
7453            Therefore it is not possible to add/set an immutable object to a mutable object.
7454        */
7455        virtual bool_t immutable() const = 0;
7456
7457    protected:
7458        /**
7459            This object can be destroyed only by the AVBlocks library.
7460        */
7461        ~MediaSocketList() {}
7462    };

7464    /**
7465        Defines the status of a transcoder operation.
7466        
7467        It is sent with the TranscoderCallback::onStatus notification.
7468    */
7469    namespace TranscoderStatus
7470    {
7471        /**
7472            TranscoderStatus::Enum
7473        */
7474        enum Enum
7475        {
7476            /** Transcoder::run has completed successfully.  */
7477            Completed = 0,
7478        };

7481    /**
7482        The TranscoderCallback provides a way to receive notifications from the Transcoder and also to control its operation 
7483        while it is running (Transcoder::run).
7484
7485        This class is meant to be inherited by the user code and only the required notifications/methods can be overridden.
7486
7487        When a TranscoderCallback instance is set (Transcoder::setCallback) it is retained by the Transcoder.
7488        The TranscoderCallback instance is released when the Transcoder itself is being destroyed.
7489        
7490        The default implementation of primo::Reference keeps a constant reference count of 1.
7491        This can be used when the user code is the sole owner of the implemented callback and does not need 
7492        to manage it through the primo::Reference interface.
7493
7494        The TranscoderCallback is used only when the transcoding is performed via Transcoder::run.
7495
7496        @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7497
7498    */
7499    class TranscoderCallback : public primo::Reference
7500    {
7501    public:
7502
7503        /**
7504            This method is called periodically by the Transcoder to report transcoding progress. See Transcoder::run.
7505            
7506            @param currentTime [in] The duration of the media stream that has been processed so far. Time is in seconds.
7507            
7508            @param totalTime [in] The total duration of the media stream that will be processed eventually. Time is in seconds.
7509
7510            For performance reasons this notification is not called for every processed media sample. 
7511            Currently it is called once for every 0.5 seconds of processed media data.
7512            This notification is intended for user interface updates.
7513
7514            The transcoding progress in percents is given by: (currentTime / totalTime * 100).
7515
7516            The Transcoder does not guarantee that currentTime will ever reach totalTime 
7517            even when the transcoding completes successfully.
7518        */
7519        virtual void onProgress(double currentTime, double totalTime)
7520        {
7521        }
7522
7523        /**
7524            This method is called by the Transcoder to report the status of current operation.
7525
7526            @param status [in] Transcoder status.
7527
7528            @see TranscoderStatus::Enum
7529        */
7530        virtual void onStatus(TranscoderStatus::Enum status)
7531        {
7532        }
7533
7534        /**
7535            This method is called by the Transcoder to give the user code a chance to stop the transcoding process 
7536            started by Transcoder::run().
7537
7538            @param currentTime [in] The duration of the media stream that has been processed so far. Time is in seconds.
7539
7540            @return TRUE if the Transcoder should continue running. FALSE if the Transcoder should stop.
7541
7542            When instructed the Transcoder stops the transcoding process gracefully so that 
7543            the media data processed is valid (playable).
7544
7545            This notification is called as often as possible so that the user code may stop the transcoding process as soon as it is required.
7546            For this reason there should be minimal processing in this method if it is overridden by the user code, 
7547            otherwise the overall transcoding may be slowed down.
7548        */
7549        virtual bool_t onContinue(double currentTime)
7550        {
7551            return 1;
7552        }
7553
7554        /**
7555            This method is called by the Transcoder when an input format has been detected or has changed.
7556            The user code has a chance to inspect detected inputs, re-configure outputs, connect or disable pins.
7557
7558            @param inputIndex [in] The index of the input socket that has changed. 
7559            The socket contains pins that describe the new format.
7560
7561            Currently this notification is used by the Transcoder when an input socket is configured without pins
7562            and the input stream is pushed via Transcoder::push().
7563            The notification is invoked when the input format is detected and after the appropriate pins are added to the input socket.
7564            The user code may inspect the input pins and can decide which pins to connect (via MediaPin::setConnection()).
7565            It may also add or remove output sockets and pins.
7566            The Transcoder is fully initialized only after all inputs have been detected and the user code returns from this method.
7567        */
7568        virtual void onInputChange(int32_t inputIndex)
7569        {
7570        }
7571
7572        /**
7573            The default implementation keeps a constant reference count of 1.
7574            
7575            @return 1
7576        */
7577        int32_t retain() const		{ return 1; }
7578
7579        /**
7580            The default implementation keeps a constant reference count of 1.
7581
7582            @return 1
7583        */
7584        int32_t release() const		{ return 1; }
7585
7586        /**
7587            The default implementation keeps a constant reference count of 1.
7588
7589            @return 1
7590        */
7591        int32_t retainCount() const	{ return 1; }
7592    };

7594    /**
7595        A Block is a unit that can produce, consume or transform media samples from/to multiple inputs/outputs
7596    */
7597    class Block : public primo::Reference
7598    {
7599        public:
7600            
7601        /**
7602        Returns a modifiable collection of MediaSocket objects which
7603        describe the input data of the block.
7604
7605        @return A pointer to a collection of input sockets. Cannot be <b>NULL</b>.
7606        */
7607        virtual MediaSocketList* inputs() const = 0;
7608
7609        /**
7610        Returns a modifiable collection of MediaSocket objects which
7611        describe the output data of the block.
7612
7613        @return A pointer to a collection of output sockets. Cannot be <b>NULL</b>.
7614        */
7615        virtual MediaSocketList* outputs() const = 0;
7616
7617        /**
7618        Initializes the block based on the specified inputs and outputs.
7619
7620        @return TRU The block is successfully initialized and is ready to process data, otherwise FALSE.
7621        */
7622        virtual bool_t open() = 0;
7623
7624        /**
7625        Pushes input data to the block.
7626
7627        @param inputIndex [in] Specifies the index of the input socket whose data is pushed to the block.
7628        
7629        @param inputSample [in] A pointer to a MediaSample object that contains the input data.
7630        
7631        @return TRUE The block has successfully processed the input data, otherwise FALSE.
7632        */
7633        virtual bool_t push(int32_t inputIndex, primo::codecs::MediaSample* inputSample) = 0;
7634
7635        /**
7636        Pulls output data from the block.
7637
7638        @param outputIndex [out] contains the index of the output socket to which the data belongs.
7639
7640        @param outputData [out] A pointer to a MediaSample object that receives the output data.
7641        
7642        @return TRUE The block has successfully generated output, otherwise FALSE.
7643        */
7644        virtual bool_t pull(int32_t& outputIndex, primo::codecs::MediaSample* outputData) = 0;
7645      
7646        /**
7647        Closes the block. When closed it can neither accept, nor deliver data.
7648        */
7649        virtual void close() = 0;
7650
7651        /**
7652        Flushes the data buffered in the block to the output.
7653        This method can be used only in push mode.
7654
7655        @return TRUE if the buffered data is successfully flushed, otherwise FALSE.
7656
7657        @remarks This method also marks the end-of-stream for all inputs.
7658        No data should be pushed to the block after it is flushed.
7659        */
7660        virtual bool_t flush() = 0;
7661
7662        /**
7663        Tells the block that there's no more data for the specified input socket.
7664        This method can be used only in push mode.
7665
7666        @param inputIndex [in] specifies the index of the input socket for which there's no more data.
7667
7668        @return TRUE if the operation is successful, otherwise FALSE.
7669        */
7670        virtual bool_t endOfStream(int32_t inputIndex) = 0;
7671
7672        /**
7673        Returns the error information for the last operation.
7674
7675        @return A pointer to an ErrorInfo object.
7676        */
7677        virtual const primo::error::ErrorInfo* error() const = 0;
7678    };

7681    /**
7682    Analyzes a file or a stream and provides information about its type and properties.
7683    */
7684    class MediaInfo: public Block
7685    {
7686    public:
7687        /**
7688        Returns a collection of StreamInfo objects describing the audio and video streams (tracks) found in the input.
7689
7690        @return A read-only collection of StreamInfo objects.
7691        Each StreamInfo object in the collection represents a stream (track) in the analyzed input.
7692
7693        Normally the caller is not required and should not release the returned object.
7694        However it is allowed to retain the collection and it will be valid even
7695        when the MediaInfo instance is destroyed.
7696        In all cases when the caller retains the returned collection it should release it when it is not needed anymore.
7697
7698        @deprecated Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::outputs instead.
7699
7700        @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7701        */
7702        PRIMO_DEPRECATED("primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::streams is deprecated. Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::outputs.")
7703        virtual primo::codecs::StreamInfoEnum* streams() const = 0;
7704
7705        /**
7706        Sets the input that should be analyzed.
7707
7708        @param filename [in] a filename as an Unicode zero terminated string. If <b>NULL</b> the filename is cleared.
7709        When not <b>NULL</b> the filename is copied internally and is not required to be valid after the method returns.
7710
7711        @deprecated Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs instead.
7712        */
7713        PRIMO_DEPRECATED("primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::setInputFile is deprecated. Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs.")
7714        virtual void setInputFile(const char_t* filename) = 0;
7715
7716        /**
7717        Returns the input file previously set via setInputFile().
7718
7719        @return A filename as an Unicode zero terminated string. Can be <b>NULL</b> if the source file is not set.
7720
7721        @deprecated Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs instead.
7722        */
7723        PRIMO_DEPRECATED("primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputFile is deprecated. Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs.")
7724        virtual const char_t* inputFile() const = 0;
7725
7726        /**
7727        Sets the input stream that should be analyzed. This is an alternative to setInputFile().
7728
7729        @param stream [in] A pointer to a \link primo::Stream Stream\endlink object. If <b>NULL</b> the input stream is cleared.
7730        Internally the \link primo::Stream Stream\endlink object is retained by MediaInfo, so it is safe to release it after this method returns.
7731
7732        MediaInfo will use the input file when both an input file and input stream are set.
7733
7734        @deprecated Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs instead.
7735
7736        @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7737        */
7738        PRIMO_DEPRECATED("primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::setInputStream is deprecated. Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs.")
7739        virtual void setInputStream(primo::Stream* stream) = 0;
7740
7741        /**
7742        Returns the input stream previously set via setInputStream().
7743
7744        @return A Stream object. Can be <b>NULL</b> if the source stream is not set.
7745
7746        @deprecated Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs instead.
7747        */
7748        PRIMO_DEPRECATED("primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputStream is deprecated. Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs.")
7749        virtual primo::Stream* inputStream() const = 0;
7750
7751        /**
7752        Forces a specific stream type.
7753
7754        @param streamType [in] stream type such as AVI, WAV, MP4, etc.
7755
7756        If the input is a file and the stream type is not set, the stream type is deduced from the filename extension.
7757        If the input is a stream, MediaInfo requires the stream type to be specified.
7758        If the stream type is set to something other than \link primo::codecs::StreamType::Unknown StreamType::Unknown\endlink,
7759        it takes precedence and is used by MediaInfo regardless of the detected stream type.
7760
7761        @deprecated Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs instead.
7762        */
7763        PRIMO_DEPRECATED("primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::setStreamType is deprecated. Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs.")
7764        virtual void setStreamType(primo::codecs::StreamType::Enum streamType) = 0;
7765
7766        /**
7767        Returns the stream type previously set via setStreamType() or the one detected by MediaInfo.
7768
7769        @return input stream type. The default value is \link primo::codecs::StreamType::Unknown StreamType::Unknown\endlink.
7770
7771        @deprecated Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs instead.
7772        */
7773        PRIMO_DEPRECATED("primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::streamType is deprecated. Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs.")
7774        virtual primo::codecs::StreamType::Enum streamType() const = 0;
7775
7776        /**
7777        Returns the stream subtype detected by MediaInfo.
7778
7779        @return input stream subtype. The default value is \link primo::codecs::StreamSubType::Unknown StreamSubType::Unknown\endlink.
7780
7781        @deprecated Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs instead.
7782        */
7783        PRIMO_DEPRECATED("primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::streamSubType is deprecated. Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::inputs.")
7784        virtual primo::codecs::StreamSubType::Enum streamSubType() const = 0;
7785
7786        /**
7787        Analyzes the input specified by setInputFile() or setInputStream() and loads the information in the MediaInfo object.
7788
7789        @return TRUE if the input is successfully analyzed, otherwise FALSE.
7790
7791        If this method is successful the information about the detected media streams (tracks) and metadata can be obtained from MediaInfo.
7792
7793        @deprecated Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::open instead.
7794
7795        @see MediaInfo::streams
7796        @see MediaInfo::metadata
7797        */
7798        PRIMO_DEPRECATED("primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::load is deprecated. Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::open.")
7799        virtual bool_t load() = 0;
7800
7801        /**
7802        Returns the metadata for the input.
7803
7804        @return A pointer to a Metadata object. Can be <b>NULL</b> if the input has no metadata.
7805
7806        Normally the caller is not required and should not release the returned object.
7807        However it is allowed to retain the Metadata object and it will be valid even
7808        when the MediaInfo instance is destroyed.
7809        In all cases when the caller retains the returned object it should release it when it is not needed anymore.
7810
7811        @deprecated Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::outputs instead.
7812
7813        @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
7814        */
7815        PRIMO_DEPRECATED("primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::metadata is deprecated. Please use primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::outputs.")
7816        virtual primo::codecs::Metadata* metadata() const = 0;
7817
7818        /**
7819        Indicates whether stream info and metadata have been loaded and parsed.
7820        @see \ref primo::avblocks::MediaInfo::push "MediaInfo::push"
7821        */
7822        virtual bool_t isReady() = 0;
7823
7824        /**
7825        Pushes input data to the <b>MediaInfo</b>.
7826
7827        @param inputIndex [in] Specifies the index of the input socket whose data is pushed to the MediaInfo. Must be zero.
7828
7829        @param inputSample [in] A pointer to a MediaSample object that contains the input data.
7830
7831        @return TRUE The <b>MediaInfo</b> has successfully processed the input data, otherwise FALSE.
7832
7833        @remarks In order to use this method the inputs()->at(0)->streamType() must be set and open() must be called.
7834
7835        @see MediaInfo::isReady
7836
7837        @note
7838        <table border="0">
7839        <tr>
7840        <td>Supported stream types:</td>
7841        <td>\link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG1_Video StreamType::MPEG1_Video\endlink</td>
7842        </tr>
7843        <tr>
7844        <td></td>
7845        <td>\link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG2_Video StreamType::MPEG2_Video\endlink</td>
7846        </tr>
7847        <tr>
7848        <td></td>
7849        <td>\link primo::codecs::StreamType::H264 StreamType::H264\endlink</td>
7850        </tr>
7851        <tr>
7852        <td></td>
7853        <td>\link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG_TS StreamType::MPEG_TS\endlink</td>
7854        </tr>
7855        </table>
7856        */
7857        virtual bool_t push(int32_t inputIndex, primo::codecs::MediaSample* inputSample) = 0;
7858
7859        /**
7860        Returns a modifiable collection of MediaSocket objects which describe the input data of the MediaInfo.
7861        The collection contains one default MediaSocket that must be configured.
7862
7863        Each socket in the collection represents an input point -
7864        it can be a container with one or more streams or just an elementary stream.
7865
7866        @return A pointer to a collection of input sockets. Cannot be <b>NULL</b>.
7867        */
7868        virtual MediaSocketList* inputs() const = 0;
7869
7870
7871        /**
7872        Returns an immutable collection of MediaSocket objects describing the audio and video streams (tracks) found in the input.
7873
7874        @return A pointer to a collection of output sockets. Cannot be <b>NULL</b>.
7875        */
7876        virtual MediaSocketList* outputs() const = 0;
7877
7878        /**
7879        Analyzes the input specified by inputs() and loads the information in the MediaInfo object.
7880
7881        @return TRUE if the input is successfully analyzed.
7882        @return FALSE if the input could not be analyzed. In this case, the error() method will return detailed error information.
7883
7884        If this method succeeds the information about the detected media streams (tracks) and metadata can be obtained from MediaInfo.
7885        */
7886        virtual bool_t open() = 0;
7887
7888    protected:
7889        /**
7890        This object can be destroyed only by the AVBlocks library.
7891        */
7892        ~MediaInfo() {}
7893    };
