7896    /**
7897        Provides functionality for audio and video encoding, decoding and transforming.
7898    */
7899    class Transcoder : public primo::avblocks::Block
7900    {
7901        public:
7902        
7903        /**
7904            Returns a modifiable collection of MediaSocket objects which
7905            describe the input data of the transcoder.
7906
7907            Each socket in the collection represents an input point -
7908            it can be a container with one or more streams or just an elementary stream.
7909
7910            @return A pointer to a collection of input sockets. Cannot be <b>NULL</b>.
7911
7912            The returned collection exists only in the context of the transcoder.
7913            The caller cannot influence the lifetime of the returned object.
7914        */
7915        virtual MediaSocketList* inputs() const = 0;
7916
7917        /**
7918            Returns a modifiable collection of MediaSocket objects which
7919            describe the output data of the transcoder.
7920
7921            Each socket in the collection describes an output point -
7922            it can be a container with one or more streams or just an elementary stream.
7923
7924            @return A pointer to a collection of output sockets. Cannot be <b>NULL</b>.
7925
7926            The returned collection exists only in the context of transcoder.
7927            The caller cannot influence the lifetime of the returned object.
7928        */
7929        virtual MediaSocketList* outputs() const = 0;
7930
7931        /**
7932            Initializes the transcoder based on the specified inputs and outputs.
7933            If this method succeeds the transcoder is ready to process data.
7934            The data flow may be driven by the following methods:
7935            <ul>
7936            <li>push() - The caller pushes input data to the transcoder.
7937            The transcoder writes the output data to a file or user stream.
7938            </li>
7939            <li>pull() - The caller pulls output data from the transcoder.
7940            The transcoder reads the input data from a file or user stream.
7941            </li>
7942            <li>push() and pull() - The caller pushes input data to the transcoder.
7943            It also pulls the output data from the transcoder.
7944            </li>
7945            <li>run() - The caller waits for the transcoding to finish.
7946            The transcoder automatically reads the input data from a file or user stream
7947            and writes the output to a file or user stream.
7948            The process runs until the input data is depleted or there's a processing error.
7949            </li>
7950            </ul>
7951            However not all stream types can be used in push or pull mode. See \ref transcoder_io for more info.
7952
7953            @return <table>
7954            <tr>
7955            <td>TRUE</td> <td>The block is successfully initialized and is ready to process data.</td>
7956            </tr>
7957            <tr>
7958            <td>FALSE</td> <td>The block cannot process the specified input and output data.</td>
7959            </tr>
7960            </table>
7961        */
7962        virtual bool_t open() = 0;
7963
7964        /**
7965            Closes the transcoder. When closed it can neither accept, nor deliver data.
7966            Inputs and outputs are not modified.
7967        */
7968        virtual void close() = 0;
7969
7970        /**
7971            Flushes the data buffered in the transcoder to the output.
7972            This method can be used only in push mode.
7973
7974            @return TRUE if the buffered data is successfully flushed, otherwise FALSE.
7975
7976            @remarks This method also marks the end-of-stream for all inputs.
7977            No data should be pushed to the transcoder after it is flushed.
7978        */
7979        virtual bool_t flush() = 0;
7980
7981        /**
7982            Tells the transcoder that there's no more data for the specified input socket.
7983            If the last input socket is stopped the transcoder flushes its internal buffers to the output.
7984            This method can be used only in push mode.
7985
7986            @param inputIndex [in] specifies the index of the input socket for which there's no more data.
7987
7988            @return TRUE if the operation is successful, otherwise FALSE.
7989        */
7990        virtual bool_t endOfStream(int32_t inputIndex) = 0;
7991
7992        /**
7993            Sets the autoConnect property of the transcoder.
7994            If autoConnect is TRUE the transcoder automatically maps input to output pins when opened.
7995
7996            @param autoConnect [in] specifies to auto connect input and output pins.
7997        */
7998        virtual void setAutoConnect(bool_t autoConnect) = 0;
7999
8000        /**
8001            Returns the autoConnect property of the transcoder.
8002
8003            @return TRUE the transcoder automatically maps input to output pins when opened.
8004        */
8005        virtual bool_t autoConnect() const = 0;
8006       
8007        /**
8008            Runs an automatic transcoding.
8009
8010            @return TRUE The transcoding has succeeded. FALSE There's a transcoding error
8011            or the run() method cannot be used with the specified inputs and outputs.
8012
8013            In order to use the run mode all input and output sockets must be associated with files or user streams.
8014            The method returns when the transcoding is finished because there's no more input data to process or
8015            when there's an error.
8016
8017            @note
8018            The input socket can specify an image file in which case the output video contains a single frame.
8019            A single frame video (MPEG-2) can be used as a background in DVD-Video authoring.
8020            For generating a custom video from many images see Transcoder::push.
8021        */
8022        virtual bool_t run() = 0;
8023
8024        // WARNING: The `Supported stream types` table must be under the `push` and `pull` methods below. 
8025        // The documentation gets ruined if there is a comment between the table and the method
8026        /**
8027            Pushes input data to the Transcoder.
8028            
8029            @param inputIndex [in] Specifies the index of the input socket whose data is pushed to the Transcoder.
8030            
8031            @param inputSample [in] A pointer to a MediaSample object that contains the input data.
8032            The MediaSample provided is used only within this method and the object is not retained by the Transcoder.
8033            It is not guaranteed that the whole input will be consumed (read) by the Transcoder after this method has returned.
8034            It's possible that the Transcoder may consume only part of the provided input data.
8035            When this method returns successfully 
8036            the \link primo::codecs::MediaBuffer::dataSize MediaBuffer::dataSize\endlink and
8037            the \link primo::codecs::MediaBuffer::dataOffset MediaBuffer::dataOffset\endlink
8038            are updated to reflect how much data is left and where it starts in the buffer.
8039            This must be taken into consideration if more data should be appended for subsequent pushing.
8040            
8041            @return TRUE The Transcoder has successfully processed some or all of the input data, otherwise FALSE.
8042            
8043            @remarks In order to use this method the input socket must not have an associated file or user stream.
8044            If the transcoder operates in the hybrid push/pull mode it will return 
8045            \ref primo::avblocks::TranscoderError::InputFull "TranscoderError::InputFull" when it cannot accept the input.
8046            In this case Transcoder::pull() must be called to retrieve the available output.
8047            
8048            @note
8049            The input sample can contain an image like bmp, png or jpeg.
8050            This makes it possible to create a video from one or more images with any duration.
8051            The start time of each input sample must be set explicitly and must increase for each successive sample.
8052
8053            @warning
8054            This method is not thread-safe (as all other functions in AVBlocks). It cannot be called simultaneously from multiple threads.
8055            You must implement your own synchronization if the method will be called from multiple threads.
8056        */
8057        virtual bool_t push(int32_t inputIndex, primo::codecs::MediaSample* inputSample) = 0;
8058        /*!<
8059            |    Supported %Stream Types                                                                |    %MediaSample format                               |
8060            |:---------------------------                                                               |:---------------------------                          |
8061            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::LPCM StreamType::LPCM\endlink                            |                                                      |
8062            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::ALAW_PCM StreamType::ALAW_PCM\endlink                    |                                                      |
8063            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MULAW_PCM StreamType::MULAW_PCM\endlink                  |                                                      |
8064            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::G726_ADPCM StreamType::G726_ADPCM\endlink                |                                                      |
8065            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::UncompressedVideo StreamType::UncompressedVideo\endlink  |                                                      |
8066            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG1_Video StreamType::MPEG1_Video\endlink              |                                                      |
8067            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG2_Video StreamType::MPEG2_Video\endlink              |                                                      |
8068            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG4_Video StreamType::MPEG4_Video\endlink              |                                                      |
8069            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::H264 StreamType::H264\endlink                            |                                                      |
8070            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MJPEG StreamType::MJPEG\endlink                          |                                                      |
8071            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG_TS StreamType::MPEG_TS\endlink                      |                                                      |
8072            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::BMP StreamType::BMP\endlink                              |                                                      |
8073            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::PNG StreamType::PNG\endlink                              |                                                      |
8074            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::JPEG StreamType::JPEG\endlink                            | See [Pushing JPEG](@ref using_transcoder_push_jpeg)  |
8075            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::TIFF StreamType::TIFF\endlink                            |                                               |
8076            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::GIF StreamType::GIF\endlink                              |                                               |
8077        */
8078
8079        /**
8080            Pulls output data from the transcoder.
8081            
8082            @param outputIndex [out] contains the index of the output socket to which the data belongs.
8083            
8084            @param outputData [out] A pointer to a MediaSample object that receives the output data.
8085            When the method returns successfully the <i>outputData</i> contains the output sample.
8086
8087            Each time output data is generated a new MediaBuffer instance is created and attached to <i>outputData</i>.
8088            The new MediaBuffer instance belongs to the caller and must be released when it is not needed anymore.
8089
8090            @return TRUE The transcoder has successfully generated output, otherwise FALSE.
8091
8092            @remarks In order to use the pull mode the output sockets must not have an associated file or user stream.
8093            If the transcoder operates in the hybrid push/pull mode it will return 
8094            \ref primo::avblocks::TranscoderError::InputNeeded "TranscoderError::InputNeeded" when needs more input data.
8095            In this case Transcoder::push() must be called to supply input data to the transcoder.
8096
8097            @warning
8098            This method is not thread-safe (as all other functions in AVBlocks). It cannot be called simultaneously from multiple threads.
8099            You must implement your own synchronization if the method will be called from multiple threads.
8100        */
8101        virtual bool_t pull(int32_t& outputIndex, primo::codecs::MediaSample* outputData) = 0;
8102        /*!<
8103            |    Supported Stream Types                                                                 |
8104			|:---------------------------                                                               |
8105            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::LPCM StreamType::LPCM\endlink                            | 
8106            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::ALAW_PCM StreamType::ALAW_PCM\endlink                    | 
8107            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MULAW_PCM StreamType::MULAW_PCM\endlink                  |
8108            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::G726_ADPCM StreamType::G726_ADPCM\endlink                |
8109            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::UncompressedVideo StreamType::UncompressedVideo\endlink  |
8110            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG1_Video StreamType::MPEG1_Video\endlink              |
8111            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG2_Video StreamType::MPEG2_Video\endlink              |
8112            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG4_Video StreamType::MPEG4_Video\endlink              |
8113            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::H264 StreamType::H264\endlink                            |
8114            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG_TS StreamType::MPEG_TS\endlink                      |
8115            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG_PSI_PACKETS StreamType::MPEG_PSI_PACKETS\endlink    |
8116            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::MPEG_TS_PACKETS StreamType::MPEG_TS_PACKETS\endlink      |
8117            | \link primo::codecs::StreamType::WAVE StreamType::WAVE\endlink                            |
8118        */
8119
8120        /**
8121            Sets a TranscoderCallback instance which is used to receive notifications from the transcoder.
8122            The TranscoderCallback is used only when the transcoding is performed via Transcoder::run.
8123
8124            @param callback [in] A pointer to TranscoderCallback object that will be invoked by the transcoder while running.
8125            It is allowed to set a <b>NULL</b> object.
8126            
8127            Internally the TranscoderCallback specified by <i>setCallback</i> is retained (if not <b>NULL</b>).
8128            The previous TranscoderCallback is released (if not <b>NULL</b>).
8129            The TranscoderCallback instance is released when the Transcoder itself is being destroyed.
8130
8131            @note
8132            If the user code inherits from TranscoderCallback but does not override primo::Reference::release() and
8133            primo::Reference::retain() it must ensure that the callback instance is valid until it is used by the transcoder.
8134            This is so because the default implementation of primo::Reference in TranscoderCallback keeps a constant reference count of 1.
8135
8136            @see TranscoderCallback
8137        */
8138        virtual void setCallback(primo::avblocks::TranscoderCallback* callback) = 0;
8139
8140        /**
8141            Returns the TranscoderCallback object that is used by the Transcoder to send notifications and events while running.
8142
8143            @return A pointer to TranscoderCallback object or <b>NULL</b> if the callback is not set.
8144        */
8145        virtual primo::avblocks::TranscoderCallback* callback() = 0;
8146        
8147        
8148        /**
8149            Returns the error information for the last operation.
8150
8151            @return A pointer to an ErrorInfo object.
8152        */
8153        virtual const primo::error::ErrorInfo* error() const = 0;
8154
8155        /**
8156            Sets whether demo mode (unlicensed transcoding) should be allowed by the Transcoder.
8157
8158            @param allowDemoMode [in] specifies whether unlicensed transcoding is allowed.
8159            
8160            @remarks The demo mode is enabled by default in the Demo release but not in the OEM release of AVBlocks.
8161            Therefore in order to test transcoding with the OEM release without a valid license the transcoder demo mode must be enabled explicitly.
8162        */
8163        virtual void setAllowDemoMode(bool_t allowDemoMode) = 0;
8164        
8165        /**
8166            Returns whether the Transcoder allows demo mode (unlicensed transcoding).
8167
8168            @return If TRUE a demo overlay (watermark) is applied when a required codec is not licensed.
8169            If FALSE the Transcoder returns an error (AVBlocksError::UnlicensedFeature) instead of applying the demo overlay 
8170            when a required codec is not licensed.
8171            
8172            @remarks The default value is TRUE in the Demo release and FALSE in the OEM release.
8173        */
8174        virtual bool_t allowDemoMode() const = 0;
8175
8176    protected:
8177        
8178        /**
8179            This object can be destroyed only by the AVBlocks library. The caller must use Reference::release.
8180
8181            @see \ref object_management "Object Management"
8182        */
8183        ~Transcoder() {}
8184    };
